questions.q: In an LC oscillator, if values of inductance and capacitance become twice and eight times, respectively, then the resonant frequency of oscillator becomes $x$ times its initial resonant frequency ${ω}_{0}$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resonance frequency of an LC oscillations circuit is stated as&

${ω}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$, here,~$LandC$~represents inductance and capacitance of circuit.

Now, when inductance and capacitance changes, i.e.,~$L^{'} = 2L$~and~$C^{'} = 8C$

Then, resonant frequency is~$\omega = \dfrac{1}{2L \times 8C} = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{LC}}$

$⇒ \omega = \dfrac{\omega0}{4}$

Thus, the value of~$x = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.q: If wattless current flows in the $AC$ circuit, then the circuit is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The current in an AC circuit containing only either a capacitor or an inductor is said to be wattless& as the& average power is zero. As wattless& current has phase difference of& $ϕ = 90 °$~with voltage, therefore power factor~$cosϕ$& will be zero.

questions.q: In the figure shown, a circuit contains two identical resistors with resistance $R = 5Ω$ and an inductance with $L = 2mH .$ An ideal battery of $15V$ is connected in the circuit. What will be the current through the battery long after the switch is closed?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
After a long time, when the growth of current in the circuit has stopped, the inductor will work as a conductor. Therefore the effective resistance of the circuit will be,&

$R = \dfrac{5}{2} = 2 . 5Ω$

Hence, the current through the circuit will be,

$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{15}{2.5} = 6A$

questions.q: In an a.c. circuit, voltage and current are given by: $V = 100\sin ( 100t ) V$ and $I = 100\sin \left(100t + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)mA$ respectively. The average power dissipated in one cycle is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Standard expression of voltage is given by, $V = {V}_{0}\sin \left(\omegat\right)$and for current is given by, $I = {I}_{0}\sin \left(\omegat +ϕ\right)$. Clearly, $ϕ$ is the phase difference here. From the given expression, $ϕ = \dfrac{π}{3}.$

Average power dissipated in one cycle is given by,

${P}_{avg} = {V}_{rms}{I}_{rms}\cos ( ϕ )$

$= \dfrac{100}{2} \times \dfrac{100 \times {10}^{- 3}}{2} \timescos \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)

=\dfrac{104}{2} \times {10}^{- 3} \times \dfrac{1}{2}

=\dfrac{10}{4} =$2 . 5W$

$

questions.q: To increase the resonant frequency in series LCR circuit,
options: Another resistance should be added in series with the first resistance.
Another capacitor should be added in series with the first capacitor
The source frequency should be decreased
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resonant frequency of an LCR circuit is given by& $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$. It does not depend on the source frequency as well as the resistance of the circuit.

Therefore, to increase the resonating frequency product of $L$ and $C$ should decrease.

By joining another capacitor in series, the equivalent capacitor will decrease.

Hence, option C is correct option.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance $C = 200pF$. It is connected to $230V$ ac supply with an angular frequency $300rads^{- 1}$. The rms value of conduction current in the circuit and displacement current in the capacitor respectively are :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By Maxwell's equation for a time varying voltage (AC voltage), both conduction and displacement currents are the same. Therefore,

${I}_{displacement} = {I}_{conduction} = \dfrac{Vrms}{XC} = \dfrac{Vrms}{\dfrac{1}{\omegaC}} = 230 \times 300 \times 200 \times {10}^{- 12} = 13 .8 \mu A$

questions.q: In the given circuit the $AC$ source has $\omega = 100rads^{- 1}$. Considering the inductor and capacitor to be ideal, what will be the current $I$ flowing through the circuit?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${Z}_{C} = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{\omegaC}\right)2 + R^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{100 \times 100 \times {10}^{- 6}}\right)2 + {100}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{{100}^{2} + {100}^{2}}$

$= 100\sqrt{2}Ω$

${Z}_{L} = \sqrt{( \omegaL{)}^{2} + R^{2}} = \sqrt{( 100 \times 0 . 5{)}^{2} + {50}^{2}} = 50\sqrt{2}Ω$

${i}_{L} = \dfrac{200}{ZL} = \dfrac{200}{50\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\text{A}$

${i}_{C} = \dfrac{200}{ZC} = \dfrac{200}{100\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\text{A}$

$cos{ϕ}_{1} = \dfrac{100}{100\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}, {ϕ}_{1} = 45 °$

$cos{ϕ}_{2} = \dfrac{50}{50\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}, {ϕ}_{2} = 45 °$

$I = \sqrt{{I}_C^{2} + {I}_L^{2}}; I = \sqrt{8 + 2}; I = \sqrt{10} = 3 . 16A$

This question is bonus as the correct answer was not available for students to mark as option in original paper by NTA.

questions.q: A resistance of $40Ω$~is connected to a source of alternating current rated $220V, 50Hz$. Find the time taken by the current to change from its maximum value to the rms value :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current in AC is of the form of& $i = {i}_{0}sin\omegat$. The maximum current is~${i}_{0}$~and rms current is~$\dfrac{i0}{2}$. The change in the phase when current change from maximum to rms value is~$\dfrac{π}{4}rad$. Therefore, the time taken for the same will be,

$t = \dfrac{∆ ϕ}{ω} = \dfrac{π}{4 \times 2\pi \times 50} = 2 . 5ms$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : When the frequency of an AC& source in a series LCR circuit increases, the current in the circuit first increases, attains a maximum value and then decreases.

Statement II : In a series LCR circuit, the value of power factor at resonance is one.

In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When an a.c. voltage is applied in a series LCR circuit, the current is increased first, attains a maximum and then decreases.

The formula to calculate the power factor is given by

$cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + \left({XL}^{2} - {XC}^{2}\right)} . . . \left($1\right)$

At resonance,~${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$, Hence,

$cos{ϕ}_{resonance} = 1$

Thus, both the statements are true.

$

questions.q: The current flowing through an ac circuit is given by& $I = 5\sin \left(120\pit\right)A$. How long will the current take to reach the peak value starting from zero?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If initial value of current is zero, then it will take& $\dfrac{T}{4}$~time to reach the peak value, where~$T =$~time period.

As we know,~$\omega = 120\pi$

Therefore,

$t = \dfrac{T}{4} = \dfrac{2\pi\omega}{4}= \dfrac{π}{2\omega} = \dfrac{π}{2 \times 120\pi} = \dfrac{1}{240}s$

Statement II: Current in a purely resistive circuit can never be less than that in a series LCR circuit when connected to same voltage source.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement-I $I_m=\frac{V_m}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2}}$ at resonance $X_L=X_C$ Thus, $I_m=\frac{V_m}{R}\because$ Impendence is minimum therefore $I$ is maximum at resonance.
Statement-II $\mathrm{I}= \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}})$in purely resistive circuit.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $150 . 0\muF$ is connected to an alternating source of emf given by $E = 36\sin \left(120\pit\right)V$. The maximum value of current in the circuit is approximately equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for maximum current is given by&

${I}_\max = \omegaC{V}_{m} . . . ( i )$

The given data is~

$\omega = 120\pi$

${V}_{m} = 36VC = 150\mu F$

Substituting the values in equation (i)

${I}_\max = \left(120\pi\right) \times \left(150 \times {10}^{- 6}\right) \times 36$

$= 2 . 036A$

$\approx 2A$

questions.q: In the given circuit, the magnitude of ${V}_{L}$ and ${V}_{C}$ are twice that of ${V}_{R}$. Given that $f = 50Hz$, the inductance of the coil is $\dfrac{1}{K\pi}mH$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since the voltage across the inductor& and capacitor is same, the circuit is in resonance. Therefore, the current in the circuit will be,

$i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{220}{5} = 44A$.

The voltage across the inductor is double that across the resistor. Therefore,~${V}_{L} = 2{V}_{R} = 440V$.

We know that~${V}_{L} = i{X}_{L} = i \times 2\pifL ⇒ L = \dfrac{440}{44 \times 100\pi} = \dfrac{1}{10\pi}H = \dfrac{100}{π}mH$

Therefore,~$K = \dfrac{1}{100} = 0 . 01 \approx 0$.

questions.q: An inductor of reactance $100 \Omega$, a capacitor of reactance $50 \Omega$, and a resistor of resistance $50 \Omega$ are connected in series with an AC source of 10 V , 50 Hz. Average power dissipated by the circuit is ________ W.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}} \cos \phi \\ & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}} \times \frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\mathrm{z}} \times \frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{z}} \\ & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 \times \frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{z}^2} \\ & \mathrm{z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{L}}-\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{C}}\right)^2} \\ & \mathrm{Z}=50 \sqrt{2} \Omega \\ & \mathrm{P}=100 \times \frac{50}{2500 \times 2}=1 \mathrm{~W}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit with $L = \dfrac{100}{π}mH, C = \dfrac{10- 3}{π}F$ and $R = 10Ω$, is connected across an AC source of $220V, 50Hz$ supply. The power factor of the circuit would be ____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The capacitive reactance of the circuit is given by,

$\begin{cases}{X}_{c} & = & \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} \\ & = & \dfrac{π}{2\pi \times 50 \times {10}^{- 3}} \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$

The inductive reactance of the circuit is given by,

$\begin{cases}{X}_{L} & = & \omegaL \\ & = & 2\pi \times 50 \times \dfrac{100}{π} \times {10}^{- 3} \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$

From above calculations, it is clear that

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$

$∴$ Power factor $= \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{R} = 1$

questions.q: An ideal transformer with purely resistive load operates at $12kV$ on the primary side. It supplies electrical energy to a number of nearby houses at~$120V .$ The average rate of energy consumption in the houses served by the transformer is $60kW .$ The value of resistive load $( {R}_{s} )$ required in the secondary circuit will be_________mΩ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

$P = 60 \times {10}^{3}W$

${V}_{s} = 120V$

A transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil.

The formula for the power delivered is given by~

$P = \dfrac{V^{2}s}{Rs}$

$⇒ 60 \times {10}^{3} = \dfrac{120 \times 120}{Rs} ⇒ {R}_{s} = \dfrac{120 \times 120}{60 \times {10}^{3}} = 240mΩ$

questions.q: In a series LCR resonant circuit, the quality factor is measured as $100$. If the inductance is increased by two fold and resistance is decreased by two fold, then the quality factor after this change will be _______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Q = \dfrac{XL}{R} = \dfrac{\omegaL}{R} = \dfrac{1}{LC}\dfrac{L}{R} = \dfrac{L}{R\sqrt{C}}$

$Q^{'} = \dfrac{2L}{ \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)\sqrt{C}} = 2\sqrt{2}Q = 2\sqrt{2}\left($100\right)$

$= 282 . 84$

$
